previous_findings_status.verification: Directly read design.md section 4, line 129; section 8, lines 387-424; and section 12, lines 585-591, against prd.md requirement 3, lines 27-33, parent design section 6, lines 194-206, and process-lifecycle.md line 8. The marker is expressly insufficient deletion authority. Cross-boot sweeping is removed. Removal requires current-invocation provenance, containment beneath the canonical staging root without a symlink/reparse-point target, an abandoned attempt, stopped and awaited writers/children, the marker, and a schema-v1 manifest matching the resolved plan/build. Partial or invalid staging and uncertain quiescence are retained with diagnostics; removal failures are structured and logged. Both installation-failure and publication-race paths refer to this same rule. Another invocation's directory is never declared stale or removed. This preserves the inherited owned, manifest-validated boundary rather than weakening it. A7 explicitly records the narrower reclamation policy and remains pending owner confirmation.

Directly read design.md section 11, lines 511-529, against section 8 step 4, lines 375-382, and prd.md AC3, lines 68-70. Separate cases now corrupt the retained Python archive and mismatch manifest.runtime_id after valid installations. The source bytes, original plan and hashes, flags, and embedded worker build remain unchanged. Each retry must identify the original derived id, return RUNTIME_INTEGRITY_FAILURE without paths, leave the fetch count at three, and create no staging directory. Snapshots taken after corruption but before retry must match post-rejection paths, entry types, bytes, permissions, and modification times; no repair, deletion, or new version is allowed. These are feasible fixture/test-harness observations and test-only filesystem comparisons; the clauses do not require production test-only hooks, reverse dependencies, or reuse-time hashing of the extracted Python tree.

Directly read design.md section 5, lines 222-285; section 6, lines 330-338; section 7, line 358; section 8, lines 426-429; and section 10, lines 470-486. Missing curl and missing tar consistently use non-retryable RUNTIME_CURL_MISSING with the tool identified; a nonzero tar exit uses RUNTIME_EXTRACT_FAILURE. Worker-version mismatch exclusively uses RUNTIME_VERSION_MISMATCH and is excluded from RUNTIME_CONFIG_INVALID. Missing/unusable binary digests after API/SUMS exhaustion, PBS API digests, and selected-wheel digests use RUNTIME_RESOLVE_FAILURE; absent/unusable plan hashes use RUNTIME_CONFIG_INVALID; byte disagreement with a usable expected digest uses RUNTIME_INTEGRITY_FAILURE. SUMS HTTP 404 is explicitly non-retryable checksum exhaustion. Other metadata/artifact transfer failures and file-copy failures use RUNTIME_DOWNLOAD_FAILURE, while unusable or ambiguous retrieved metadata uses RUNTIME_RESOLVE_FAILURE. Only RUNTIME_DOWNLOAD_FAILURE receives the three-attempt, 2s/4s retry policy. The body and table now agree without an overlapping missing-checksum or missing-tool outcome.

Directly read design.md section 11, lines 513 and 531-560, against prd.md requirement 1 and AC1. The documented offline procedure requires an owner-recorded delivery commit C after implementation review and gates, followed by reviewer inspection before final acceptance/push. It specifies an ancestry check from c08f398, enumeration and patch inspection of relevant intervening commits including merge parents, and inspection of C's parent-to-result transition and file contents. Assertions bind installer introduction and wiring, sole boot replacement, LibraryInstaller/import/helper removal, Cargo.toml dependency/patch removal, and matching Cargo.lock changes to that single transition. The parent must retain the old path; earlier partial deliveries invalidate acceptance even if the final tree passes metadata checks. This supplies the missing mechanical history check. The procedure was reviewed as text, not executed, and no future delivery commit is claimed to have passed it.

A6: A pinned wheel plus ZIP extraction supplies the Python package closure; a future pin with hard runtime dependencies requires additional pinned wheels. Inline: design.md section 5, lines 295-297; definition: section 12, lines 581-584. Inline count: 1. Closure of G5 confirms traceability, not the runtime sufficiency of an untested future pin.

A7: Proposed conservative staging cleanup, pending owner confirmation. Inline: design.md section 8, lines 406-424; definition: section 12, lines 585-591. Inline count: 1. Automatic removal is limited to this invocation's owned, manifest-validated staging after abandonment and confirmed writer/child quiescence. No cross-boot or cross-invocation sweep occurs; partial/unvalidated staging and uncertain ownership/liveness are retained. This preserves the PRD/parent safety boundary but leaves crash residue and failed pre-manifest attempts on disk, potentially accumulating across retries and boots. The tradeoff is explicit and internally consistent; PASS does not approve A7. Owner confirmation and a revised lock remain separate steps.
No additional unmarked or untraceable decision was found within the G1-G5 fixes. This closure pass does not reopen unrelated design decisions.
